healthcareSystem: Universal (SUS — Sistema Único de Saúde, free for all; tourists can access but expect long waits). Private healthcare (plans de saúde) provides faster, higher-quality care for those who can pay.
qualityNotes: Public healthcare (SUS) is free but often overcrowded with long wait times. Private hospitals in major cities (São Paulo, Rio, Brasília) offer excellent care comparable to Western standards. Many private doctors speak English. Pharmacies (Farmácias) are everywhere.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 7am-11pm; 24-hour pharmacies available in major cities; chains include Drogaria São Paulo, Pague Menos, and Raia
pharmacyTips: Many medications available OTC that require prescriptions in the US. Pharmacists are helpful. Bring a list with generic names. Dengue and Zika prevention: bring insect repellent with DEET. Sunscreen is expensive — bring your own.
prescriptionRules: A Brazilian prescription is required for prescription medications. Foreign prescriptions are not accepted. Antibiotics and many other drugs are widely available OTC. Carry medications in original packaging with a doctor's note.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD stimulant medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Stimulants are controlled substances. Bring original prescription, doctor's letter, and carry only personal-use quantities. Declare to customs if carrying controlled substances.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is controlled. Some products may be available with prescription. Carry alternatives if possible.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications (diazepam, alprazolam, etc.)
restrictedMeds.note: Benzodiazepines require documentation. Carry a doctor's letter explaining medical necessity.

restrictedMeds.name: Methylphenidate (Ritalin/Concerta)
restrictedMeds.note: Bring documentation and only the amount needed for your stay.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in Portuguese or English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. For controlled substances, carry original prescriptions and a note explaining medical necessity. Portuguese translation of prescriptions is helpful.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: NOT legally required for entry, but strongly recommended. SUS is free but public hospitals are overcrowded — serious medical issues require private care which is expensive without insurance.
travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance is essential. Private hospital care can cost $1,000-$5,000+/day. Medical evacuation coverage is important, especially in the Amazon region. Ensure coverage includes tropical diseases (dengue, Zika, yellow fever complications). COVID-19 coverage is also advisable.

recommended: Yellow Fever (required for travel to certain states/regions; recommended for Amazon and rural areas; some areas require proof of vaccination)
vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever vaccination is required or strongly recommended depending on region — check current requirements for your specific destinations. Especially important for Amazon basin, Pantanal, and parts of Minas Gerais, São Paulo, and Rio states. Get vaccinated at least 10 days before travel.

waterNotes: Tap water is generally safe in major cities like São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, but bottled water is recommended in smaller towns and rural areas. Avoid tap water in the Northeast region and rural Amazon. Use bottled water for brushing teeth if unsure.
foodSafetyTips: In restaurants and hotels, food is generally safe. Be cautious with street food vendors. Avoid raw salads or unpeeled fruits from informal vendors. In tourist areas of Rio, São Paulo, and coastal resorts, restaurants maintain good hygiene. Be cautious with seafood from street vendors.
medicalTourismNote: Brazil is a well-known medical tourism destination, particularly for cosmetic surgery (Brazil is world-renowned for plastic surgery). Costs in private clinics are 50-70% lower than in the US. Popular destinations include São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and Porto Alegre. Choose JCI-accredited hospitals.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Brazil. Emergency numbers (192/190/193), pharmacy tips, yellow fever vaccination, restricted medications, and travel insurance advice.
